samples_reviewed.question_text: A triangle has sides 2 cm, 1 cm, and 2 cm. What is its perimeter?
A rectangle has sides 5 cm and 12 cm. What is its perimeter?

Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.

How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.

Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sentence puts perimeter of a plane figure at the centre, and only six of the sixteen samples get there: seed 604 'A triangle has sides 2 cm, 4 cm, and 4 cm. What is its perimeter?' (10), seed 603 'A square has a side of 3 cm. What is its perimeter?' (12), seed 46 'A rectangle has sides 7 cm and 1 cm. What is its perimeter?' (16), plus seeds 42, 43 and 601, and all six are arithmetically right. The remaining ten name no figure and no perimeter at all: seeds 44, 45, 50, 501 and 502 read 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.', seeds 68 and 500 read 'How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.', and seed 606 is 'Which is longer: 2 cm or 12 cm?'. Length measurement is a fair reading of using appropriate tools, but a pool where the majority of items never reach a perimeter under-delivers the stated skill.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sentence names two actions on one object, identify and measure the perimeter. Measuring is present but only ever on a single object, as in seed 45 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.'; no sample asks a student to apply a tool around a plane figure. The perimeter items instead hand the lengths over already, as in seed 42 'A triangle has sides 2 cm, 1 cm, and 2 cm. What is its perimeter?', so nothing measures a perimeter. No item asks a student to identify which measure is the perimeter, so the identify verb is unrepresented. Shape coverage inside the perimeter items is good: triangle at seeds 42 and 604, rectangle at seeds 43, 46 and 601, square at seed 603. Both triangles can exist: 1+2>2 for seed 42 and 2+4>4 for seed 604, so each obeys the triangle inequality on all three pairings.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Every item is a single step at grade 2 depth: one sum of three small sides at seed 604 'A triangle has sides 2 cm, 4 cm, and 4 cm. What is its perimeter?', one doubling at seed 603 'A square has a side of 3 cm. What is its perimeter?', or one direct reading at seed 44 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.'. No sample chains two operations, needs a formula, or asks for an unknown side, and the vocabulary stays at perimeter, longer, centimeters and meters.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The sixteen samples spread across three formatters (mcq at seed 46, cloze at seed 50, read_mcq at seed 68) and five genuinely different framings: direct perimeter of a stated figure at seed 603 'A square has a side of 3 cm. What is its perimeter?', tool reading at seed 44 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.', unit choice at seed 605 'Which unit would you use to measure the distance between the barangay hall and the plaza: centimeters or meters?', length comparison at seed 606 'Which is longer: 2 cm or 12 cm?', and a fencing context at seed 601 'A rectangular garden is 11 cm long and 10 cm wide.'. Distractor spacing also varies rather than being fixed at plus or minus one.

competency_alignment.rationale: Two samples sit outside the sentence rather than short of it. Seed 606 'Which is longer: 2 cm or 12 cm?' compares two bare numbers with no figure and no tool, and seed 607 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 22 cm.' likewise only ranks two given distances. Neither identifies nor measures a perimeter, and neither involves a plane figure; they are prior length-comparison work rather than this sentence. Seed 605 on choosing centimeters or meters is defensible under using appropriate tools, so it is not counted here.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Magnitudes are implausible for the objects named in five samples, and they contradict the unit sense this same node teaches. Seeds 500, 501 and 502 ask 'How long is the object? Give your answer in cm.' and 'Measure the object. Its length is ___ cm.' with answers of 409, 328 and 259 centimetres, that is two to four metres, with distractors a single centimetre apart, which no grade 2 ruler can resolve. Seed 607 'The distance from the bench to the tree is 22 cm.' places two landmarks a hand-span apart, and seed 601 'A rectangular garden is 11 cm long and 10 cm wide.' is a garden smaller than a sheet of paper. Seed 605 in the same pool asks 'Which unit would you use to measure the distance between the barangay hall and the plaza: centimeters or meters?', so the pool rewards choosing metres for a long distance while modelling gardens and landmark distances in centimetres. The arithmetic is sound throughout; the defect is the object-to-unit pairing.
